title: Both, either, neither, so, nor
subtitle: Talking about two things, and adding so / nor

rows.use: To emphasise that each of two things is true
rows.example: **Both** Adam and Vicky said Colin was very kind. Simon is **both** rude and unkind.

rows.use: To say the same thing about two things
rows.example: My sister and I were **both** shocked by what you said. Jack and Jill **both** know lots of jokes.

items: We sometimes use **of** with **both**. We always use this when it comes before a pronoun.
I used to be good friends with Lisa and Mike, but I've had an argument with **both of them**.

blocks.text: Form: **either** + noun + **or** + noun · **either** + adjective + **or** + adjective · **either** + verb + **or** + verb

rows.use: To talk about a choice between two things
rows.example: I think I'll buy a Valentine's card with **either** a puppy **or** a kitten on it. I'm not sure how Tom will react — he'll be **either** happy **or** shocked! You can **either** tell him how you feel **or** hope he notices.

items: We sometimes use **of** with **either**. We always use this when it comes before a pronoun.
I really like Robert and Martin — I'll go out with **either of them**!

blocks.text: Form: **neither** + noun + **nor** + noun · **neither** + adjective + **nor** + adjective · **neither** + verb + **nor** + verb

rows.use: To emphasise that each of two negative things is true
rows.example: I've got **neither** the time **nor** the energy to take up a new hobby at the moment. What you said to Lucy was **neither** true **nor** fair.

items: We sometimes use **of** with **neither**. We always use this when it comes before a pronoun.
**Neither of** us found Jason's joke funny.

rows.use: To add more information to a positive statement
rows.example: Lisa is really unkind, and **so is** Angela. You're good at listening to people, and **so am I**.

rows.use: To add more information to a negative statement
rows.example: My brother hasn't been invited to the party, and **nor has** his friend. Tom wouldn't forgive Jenny if she told everyone his secret, and **nor would I**.

blocks.intro: You can also use these structures on their own in a conversation.
items: 'I like Hannah's sense of humour.' '**So do I.**'
'I don't find Mark funny.' '**Nor do I.**'

exercises.instruction: If the phrase in bold in each sentence is correct, write it again. If it is wrong, write the correct phrase.

items.prompt: I was surprised that **both and Mary and Oliver** were late for the meeting.
